rationale: The pathway change is already approved for every patient, so the useful question is what it costs and what follows from it, not whether it works in a controlled sense. A cost-consequence analysis compares the 2026 and 2027 trial episodes from the health service and patient perspectives, lists unplanned attendances, infections and on-time implant decisions beside the costs (claims c1 and c2), prices contacts with local unit costs (claim c3 gives the planning values), and counts travel and companion time, which the retrieved evidence suggests is the larger share (claim c4). Reporting follows CHEERS 2022.
alternatives: Cost-utility analysis with quality-adjusted life years (refused: no utility measurement exists for 2026 and a trial week is too short for utility change to register)
Randomised comparison of telephone and clinic review (refused: the pathway is approved for all patients from January 2027)
Count of clinic slots released only (refused: ignores consequences and patient costs)
whyNotMoreComplex: A modelled cost-utility analysis would need utilities and long-term implant outcomes that neither year recorded; a transparent comparison of observed costs and consequences answers the manager's question with the data that exist.

decision.statement: Run a cost-consequence analysis of the telephone day 3 review against the in-person day 3 visit, comparing spinal cord stimulator trials in 2026 with those in 2027 from the health service and patient perspectives, with unplanned attendances and infections reported as consequences rather than folded into one number.
decision.question: Should the pain service evaluate the costs and consequences of replacing the day 3 visit with a telephone review, and from which perspectives?

criteria.text: Replacing the mid-trial visit has not been followed by more unplanned attendances elsewhere, and a telephone review costs less per contact than a clinic appointment.
Patient and companion costs are large enough to matter to the result.
The service has already costed the pathway change including patient costs.

gates.requirement: Research office determination of the evaluation's review route
gates.evidence: Service evaluation determination SE-2026-077 dated 2026-09-10, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Local unit costs for clinic slots and emergency department attendances
gates.evidence: Finance department costing memo FIN-PM-2026-14, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Count the clinic slots released and report nothing else
Health service costs only, without patient and companion costs
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c4, each from a retrieved record, and on two investigator-supplied records for the gates.

summary: Cost-consequence analysis recommended; the decision rests on four ledger claims and both gates are met on investigator-supplied records.
